newsitem.title: CHINA: China to sign coal, power plant pacts -- paper.
newsitem.headline: China to sign coal, power plant pacts -- paper.

text.p: China will sign agreements with foreign firms to develop coal mines and power plants in projects that will require total investment of nearly $6 billion, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.
The accords will be signed at a trade symposium in Xiamen in southeastern China's Fujian province this week, the newspaper said.
Companies from Germany, the United States and Israel would be involved in projects to build five coal-fired power plants worth a total of $1.8 billion, the newspaper said.
Most of the new plants would be built near coal mines, though it gave no further details.
Other projects would include four coal slurry pipelines worth $3.34 billion and an $800 million joint venture open-pit coal mine, it said.
The newspaper did not name any of the companies involved.

China's demand for energy has surged along with its rapid economic development. This has turned China -- once a net oil exporter -- into a net importer, and Beijing has been struggling to develop other energy sources to reduce its dependence on foreign petroleum.
Output of coal in 1995 was 1.298 billion tonnes compared with 219 million tonnes in 1990.

China has set foreign cooperation in the coal sector as one of its key objectives under the current five-year plan which runs through the year 2000, the newspaper quoted Vice Minister of Coal Industry Pu Hongjiu as saying.
Beijing has said it would invest a total of 145 billion yuan ($17.5 billion) in the coal industry between 1996 and 2000.
